headline: Stormy winds and rain forecast for 6 districts by noon on September 1st, warns Met Office
summary: The Bangladesh Meteorological Department predicted temporary gusty or stormy winds of 45-60 km/h, along with rain or thundershowers, in six coastal districts on Tuesday, September 1st.
details: The Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) issued a forecast for six districts, predicting temporary gusty or stormy winds. These winds were expected to blow at speeds of 45 to 60 kilometers per hour.

Along with the strong winds, these areas were also likely to experience rain or thundershowers. The forecast covered the period from 5 AM to 1 PM on Tuesday, September 1st, specifically for the country's internal river ports.
The districts under this forecast included Khulna, Barishal, Patuakhali, Noakhali, Chattogram, and Cox's Bazar. The winds were anticipated to come from the south or south-east direction.
In light of these conditions, river ports in the affected areas were advised to hoist cautionary signal number 1. This signal indicates that vessels should be aware of potential squalls.

The districts under this forecast included Khulna, Barishal, Patuakhali, Noakhali, Chattogram, and Cox's Bazar. The winds were anticipated to come from the south or south-east direction.

headline: Bangladesh approves largest pay hike since independence, doubling top salaries
summary: The new National Pay Scale 2026 will increase the lowest pay by a record 142% and cover 24 lakh civilian and military employees, along with 9.25 lakh retirees and other eligible recipients.
details: The Bangladesh government has approved the largest pay hike for civil service since independence, doubling the basic salary of top officials and raising the lowest pay by a record 142 percent. This marks the first salary revision under the new administration, following the last national pay scale introduced in 2015.

Endorsed at a cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, the National Pay Scale 2026 will be implemented in four phases between July 1, 2026, and January 1, 2028. The phased rollout is estimated to require an additional Tk 1,05,580 crore annually.

The new structure will cover 24 lakh civilian and military employees, along with 9.25 lakh retirees and other eligible recipients. The highest basic salary will rise from Tk 78,000 to Tk 1,56,000, while the lowest jumps from Tk 8,250 to Tk 20,000.

Salaries in Grades 1-11 will double, and Grades 12-20 will see increases ranging from 115 to 142 percent, narrowing the ratio between the lowest and highest grades from 1:9.45 to 1:7.8. The pay hike aims to strengthen financial security, boost motivation, and build a more efficient administration.

New benefits include Tk 3,000 monthly allowances for children with disabilities, and mobile allowances, previously limited to Grade 5 and above, will now extend across all 20 grades. A separate committee has been formed for the judicial service, with its pay scale to be approved retrospectively from July 1, 2026.

For employees in Grades 10-20, a 50% basic salary increase takes effect from July 1, 2026, followed by 25% from January 2027, and the remaining 25% from July 2027. Officials in Grades 1-9 will see a 40% increase from July 2026, 30% from January 2027, and the final 30% from July 2027, with all other allowances revised by January 1, 2028.

The government is also committed to implementing a One Rank One Pension (OROP) system in phases by 2030, given substantial financial implications and data absence. As an interim measure, net pensions will significantly increase on a slab basis, with up to a 100% rise for those receiving Tk 9,000 or less per month.

Mustafizur Rahman of the Centre for Policy Dialogue called the move logical, noting that government employees had worked under the same pay scale for 11 years, during which inflation nearly doubled. He described it as a "bold step" considering the government's fiscal constraints.
